source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 4:14 (the initial letters)
claim_en: ki daber YEDABER HU VE-GAM HINE ('that he will surely SPEAK — HE; AND BEHOLD, he...'): the INITIAL LETTERS of the four words yedaber-hu-vegam-hine spell the FOUR-LETTER NAME — checked mechanically (yod, he, vav, he) — 'to tell you that He handed the Name and all its epithets to AARON too' (the Kitzur): the run's twin crowns close — at the name-QUESTION the Name stands in the FINALS (3:13, exo_03's marquee), and at the answer that appoints the brother's mouth it stands in the INITIALS: the letter gives Aaron the Name in the verse that gives him the office.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 4:2 (the Masorah's fifteen; the Ramah; Shemot Rabbah)
claim_en: MA-ZE ve-yadekha ('WHAT IS THIS in your hand?'): written as ONE WORD (מזה, no he after the mem — the Ramah: 'one word written, two read') — one of the Masorah's FIFTEEN words written-one-read-two (the sign-list at Chronicles named); the stream carries the pair in its two-token convention — the unpointed written-form and the pointed reading beside it (both layers asserted; the written token checked); and Shemot Rabbah reads the fusion: MI-ZE — 'from THIS in your hand you are due the lash' (the staff that will strike the striker — the readings' warning to the doubter of 4:1): one word to the eye, two to the mouth, and the homily lives in the seam.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 4:3 (the printer corrected; the Ramah's eight-lean list — a stream-split carried named)
claim_en: HASHLIKHEHU artza ('THROW IT to the ground'): the PRINTER erred setting it lean — MS restores the FULL yod with the Masorah note, Minchat Kohen's full-list, the precise manuscripts, and the Ramah's explicit ruling ('hashlikhehu artza — full yod written'): the census verifies the command-token unique and the stream carries it FULL (checked); and the verse's SECOND throw-word carries a genuine SPLIT, named never merged: the Ramah's whole-Torah rule ('every throw-form with the lamed on chiriq is full — except eight, among them va-yashlikhehu artza HERE') and Minchat Kohen's lean-reading stand against the STREAM, which writes the second token full as well (the lean form's census empty — asserted): the chain's eight-lean list and the stream's letter part company at one yod, and the corpus carries both records side by side (dual-track law).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 4:24 (the Masorah's pair)
claim_en: va-YIFGESHEHU ('and He/he MET him'): exactly TWICE in Scripture — and BOTH tokens inside this one chapter (census checked): the LORD met him at the lodging-place AND SOUGHT TO KILL HIM (4:24, the circumcision-crisis) and Aaron met him at the mountain of God AND KISSED HIM (4:27) — the Kitzur binds the pair: 'when Moses was lax about the circumcision, Wrath and Fury came to swallow him — and he could not withstand them until Aaron came and helped him: BY AARON'S MERIT he was saved' — the same rare verb carrying the attack and the rescue: met to be killed, met to be kissed, eleven verses apart.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 4:12 (the Ramah against the printed margin); Kitzur on 4:12/15
claim_en: ve-HORETIKHA ('and I will TEACH YOU what you shall speak'): the Great Rabbinic Bible's margin reports 'one book writes it short, and a unique-note on it' — and MS rules: 'do NOT rely on that report' — all the books, the Hilleli copy, and the Ramah explicitly ('full vav and TWO yods written'): the stream carries the two-yod token, Torah-unique (census checked); its five crowns named ('I will teach you — by the five fifths of Torah I will give you'); and its sibling at 4:15 (ve-HORETI, 'and I will teach' the two of you) is likewise Torah-unique (asserted), with the Kitzur's Samuel-pair named ('I will teach you the GOOD and straight way' — He taught them the way, and they did not err in it): the teach-word enters the Torah twice, both times at the mouth-appointment.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 4:31 (the Masorah's pair)
claim_en: va-YAAMEN ha-am ('and the people BELIEVED'): the believed-word's ONE Torah token (census checked), its Scripture-twin at AKHISH believing David — and the Kitzur's frame: 'two good SHEPHERDS stood for Israel, Moses and David... faithful shepherds, therefore they were believed' (Moses' erase-me-from-Your-book and David's let-Your-hand-be-on-me named as the shepherds' credential); and the verse seals the run's password-file in the people's own hearing: ki FAQAD YHWH — 'that the LORD had VISITED' — the visit-verb sounding over the bowed heads exactly as the elders-script promised (3:16, the four-station file): the objection of 4:1 ('they will not believe') is refuted by the letter's own rare word.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 4:11 (the future tense)
claim_en: mi YASUM ilem ('who MAKES dumb'): the make-word in the FUTURE form — its ONE Torah token (census checked) — and the Kitzur reads the tense: 'it does not say WHO SET (sam) but WHO WILL SET (yasum) — for the future: the lying lips will be MADE DUMB at the day of judgment, and they will find no answer' (the false mouths of the psalm named): in the verse where God claims the mouth-faculties (dumb, deaf, seeing, blind — the four offices), the letter shifts one verb to the future and the chain hears the last court in it.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 4:19 (the unique lean); Kitzur's rival two-count (named)
claim_en: lekh SHUV mitzrayim ('go, RETURN to Egypt'): the return-imperative written LEAN — 'the whole Torah full, and this one lean' (MS) — while the Kitzur's Masorah counts TWO lean with the seven-journeys midrash ('shuv seven times — seven times Moses went to Egypt and returned'): the two counts carried NAMED, never merged (the run's count-dispute class); the stream's skeleton-census printed honestly: the bare shin-bet form stands three times in the Torah (Abraham's returning Gen 18:33, the dwell-imperative of Gerar Gen 20:15 — homographs of other verbs — and the return-imperative here, the DB's own reading shuv; checked in-stream): the go-back order thinned at the verse that also retires the death-threat ('all the men who sought your life have died' — exo_02's seeking, receipted).

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 4:8/13/16/21/30 (the accent-and-dot file)
claim_en: The chapter's accent-and-dot file, MS's rulings against the stream's own marks: yihye-LEKHA le-fe ('he shall be a MOUTH for you') — the lamed DAGESHED (checked); shelach-NA (4:13) — the shin on its lifting-stroke and the lamed on the lengthening-stroke in precise manuscripts (named); ve-haya HU (4:16) — fore-stressed (named); lifne faro (4:21) — 'on the WHEEL-MARK, not the hyphen': the wheel-mark-against-joining-stroke class's next station (the stream reads the joining stroke — split carried named, the accents-as-arbiters file); aharon ET (4:30) — 'WITHOUT the pause-line': the pause-line file's negative station (below the token-layer, named); ha-ACHARON (4:8, 'the latter sign') — full vav with the precise manuscripts and the old print (asserted): six rulings carried, the checkable ones checked.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 4:6 (the bosom-file; David named)
claim_en: have-na yadekha be-CHEQEKHA ('bring, pray, your hand into your BOSOM'): the your-bosom word stands THREE times in the Torah (census checked: Sarai's wrong-be-upon-you at Hagar's giving Gen 16:5, the leprous-hand sign here, and Moses' did-I-conceive-this-people at Num 11:12 — the nurse's bosom); the Kitzur's Scripture-file pairs the sign with DAVID'S bosom-verses ('as Moses was struck with the skin-whiteness, so David was struck — six months, as the sages expound'): the hand that will carry the staff learns in the bosom what the plagues will teach on Egypt — the sign is a mercy-scaled preview (in and out, white and whole, one verse each).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 4:6 (the bring-word chain)
claim_en: HAVE ('BRING'): the Kitzur's three-station chain — by JOSEPH'S bring-word Israel came to Egypt ('bring the men to the house,' Gen 43:16), by MOSES' bring-word here they leave it ('bring your hand'), and by the city-bring they will yet be gathered to Jerusalem ('the city joined together' named): the chain reads the whole descent-and-ascent between three imperatives of one verb (the station checked in-stream; the stream's fuller Torah census of the skeleton printed in-script — the priestly muster-verses of Numbers share the letters, named): the hand brought into the bosom is the door out.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 4:2/17/18 (the staff-and-elders files)
claim_en: ve-et ha-MATE ha-ze ('and THIS STAFF you shall take in your hand'): the Kitzur's crown-file on the staff-word — 'five crowns: for he is the NINTH righteous to hold the staff' — the chain of holders named whole (Adam, Enoch, Noah, Shem, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses: the staff as the corpus's oldest relay-baton; crowns are letter-ornament beyond the stream — named); the staff-gematria of the one-word what-is-this (forty seah; the twelve-tribes reading) named; and el YETER chotno (4:18, 'to JETHRO his father-in-law') — the Kitzur's pair with the exile-elders ('to the REMNANT of the elders of the exile'): 'Jethro merited that his sons' sons sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone' — the Sanhedrin from the priest of Midian (the station checked in-stream): the tools and the in-laws both filed as dynasties.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 4:22-23; Minchat Shai (named-only remainder)
claim_en: BENI VEKHORI yisrael ('MY SON, MY FIRSTBORN — Israel'): the my-firstborn word's exact Torah-PAIR (the stream's census, checked): JACOB'S to Reuben — the firstborn DEMOTED in the testament ('Reuben, my firstborn... unstable as water, you shall not excel,' Gen 49:3, gen_72) — and GOD'S to Israel here: the nation named My-firstborn in a SCRIPT handed to Moses on the road: 'and I will say to you: send My son, and you refuse — behold, I kill YOUR son, YOUR firstborn' (4:23): the script's receipt-horizon armed at the midnight-announcement (11:4-5) and the stroke itself (12:29 — the firstborn-strike the run's all-full strike-word already carries, exo_03); the named-only remainder filed: the purpose-clause of the drill ('that they may BELIEVE,' 4:5 — the sign aimed at 4:1's objection); the conditional third sign (4:9 — the Nile-water on the dry land, never narrated for the people: the letter leaves the water-sign to the plagues); the HARDENING file opens (4:21 've-ani achazeq et libo' — the readings' freewill-court convened and NOT ruled: carried open); the blood-bridegroom's two sayings (4:25-26 — the referent split named, never merged); and Jethro's LEKH LE-SHALOM ('go in peace' — the readings: the whole errand blessed in two words).
